waste_categories.description: Includes bottles, bags, wrappers, containers, and other packaging made from plastic polymers. Plastic waste is one of the most common and slow-decomposing forms of waste, taking hundreds of years to break down naturally.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Clean and dry plastics (PET bottles, HDPE containers) can be recycled into new bottles, fibers for clothing, or construction materials. Look for the recycling code (1-7) on the item to check if your local facility accepts it.
waste_categories.recommendation: Rinse containers before disposal, remove caps/labels if required, and segregate by plastic type where possible.
waste_categories.suggestion: Switch to reusable bags, steel/glass bottles, and avoid single-use plastic cutlery to reduce plastic waste generation at the source.

waste_categories.description: Discarded electronic devices such as mobile phones, batteries, computers, chargers, and household appliances that contain hazardous materials like lead, mercury, and cadmium.
waste_categories.recycle_details: E-waste must be handed over to authorized e-waste recyclers or collection centers, where valuable metals (gold, copper, silver) are extracted and hazardous parts are safely disposed of.
waste_categories.recommendation: Never throw e-waste in regular household bins. Wipe personal data from devices before recycling and remove batteries separately.
waste_categories.suggestion: Donate working electronics, repair instead of replacing when possible, and buy from brands offering take-back/recycling programs.

waste_categories.description: Kitchen scraps, vegetable peels, food leftovers, garden waste, and other naturally decomposing matter.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Can be converted into nutrient-rich compost through composting or vermicomposting, or processed in biogas plants to generate energy.
waste_categories.recommendation: Segregate wet waste separately from dry waste at the source; avoid mixing with plastics or chemicals.
waste_categories.suggestion: Start a home compost bin, use kitchen waste for organic fertilizer, and plan meals to reduce food wastage.

waste_categories.description: Newspapers, cardboard boxes, office paper, notebooks, and packaging materials made of paper.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Clean, dry paper and cardboard can be recycled into new paper products, packaging, or egg cartons. Avoid recycling paper that is heavily soiled with food or oil.
waste_categories.recommendation: Flatten cardboard boxes to save space, keep paper dry, and separate glossy/laminated paper as it's harder to recycle.
waste_categories.suggestion: Go digital where possible, reuse paper for notes/printing on both sides, and buy recycled paper products.

waste_categories.description: Bottles, jars, and broken glassware made from silica-based materials.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Glass is 100% recyclable and can be melted down repeatedly without losing quality, turned into new bottles, jars, or construction materials like glass wool.
waste_categories.recommendation: Wrap broken glass safely before disposal to protect waste handlers, and separate by color (clear, green, brown) if required locally.
waste_categories.suggestion: Reuse glass jars for storage, choose glass packaging over plastic when possible, and donate usable glassware.

waste_categories.description: Cans, foils, scrap metal, and metallic containers such as aluminum and steel items.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Metals can be melted and reformed into new products with minimal quality loss, saving significant energy compared to producing new metal from ore.
waste_categories.recommendation: Rinse food residue from cans, flatten to save space, and keep separate from other dry waste for easier processing.
waste_categories.suggestion: Buy products in aluminum/steel packaging where recycling infrastructure is strong, and recycle scrap metal through certified scrap dealers.

waste_categories.description: Includes paints, pesticides, chemicals, batteries, and cleaning agents that are toxic, corrosive, flammable, or reactive.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Must be disposed of through designated hazardous waste collection drives or facilities; should never be poured down drains or mixed with regular trash.
waste_categories.recommendation: Store in original, labeled containers until disposal and keep away from children and pets.
waste_categories.suggestion: Buy only the quantity needed, choose eco-friendly/non-toxic alternatives, and participate in community hazardous-waste collection days.

waste_categories.description: Used syringes, medicines, bandages, and other waste generated from healthcare activities at home or clinics.
waste_categories.recycle_details: Cannot be recycled through normal channels; must be handed over to pharmacies, hospitals, or designated biomedical waste collection services for safe incineration or treatment.
waste_categories.recommendation: Never dispose of medicines or sharps in regular household trash; use puncture-proof containers for needles.
waste_categories.suggestion: Return unused medicines to pharmacies through take-back programs and ask your local clinic about safe disposal options.

general_recommendations: Follow the 3 R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle — in that order of priority.
Segregate waste at the source into wet (biodegradable), dry (recyclable), and hazardous categories.
Compost organic waste at home whenever possible to reduce landfill burden.
Support local recycling and e-waste collection drives in your community.
Avoid single-use plastics and choose durable, reusable alternatives.
